363	When it's good for you, it's because HaShem loves you. When it's bad, God forbid,
364	that too is because HaShem loves you and wants to correct
365	you, cleanse you, and atone for whatever needs atoning.
366	In any case, always hold on to this explanation: that
367	tzedakah comes from HaShem's love, and mishpat comes from HaShem's love.
368	And this is what Avraham Avinu taught his children, that this is
369	the way of HaShem. Take everything to this point: no
370	matter what, the root of everything and the goal of everything is
371	love. See what Rabbeinu writes in Likutei Moharan, Torah
372	4.
373	The essence of da'at. What is da'at? It is the unity of chesed
374	and gevurah. So it is brought in the writings of the Ari z"l.
375	Da'at is the unity of chesed and gevurah. That is called da'at. Rabbeinu
376	writes, that is to say,
377	that one should not separate chesed from din, and should bless over all of them
378	"the Good, who does good."
379	And Rabbeinu writes here: "one Name" equals
380	"ahavah" in gematria. That is, both the Name HaShem, which is mercy,
381	as we said, HaShem, HaShem is mercy, and also His Name, which is the aspect of
382	Elokim ("In the beginning Elokim created"; later, "on the day
383	HaShem Elokim made"), both the Name HaShem, which is mercy, and His Name
384	which is Elokim,
385	the aspect of din: all of it is for your good, out of the love that the Holy One,
386	blessed be He, has for you. The reason for everything is
387	love, the chesed too.
388	Because even though a person says, "Clearly chesed is because
389	HaShem loves me." No, a person might think chesed is because
390	I deserve it, because I'm a tzaddik or gifted, materially
391	or spiritually, I did enough, I did a lot, I am
392	worthy of it. That too is a mistake. No, all the good things
393	that come to you are not because of your talents. They are gifts from HaShem.
394	>> It's not merit.
395	>> Right, it's not a reward. They are gifts from
396	HaShem. And the din upon us is also gifts,
397	gifts we don't appreciate, but they are gifts, as
398	it is written: "For whom HaShem loves He rebukes."
